science.headline:
How Peptide Therapy
Differs From Supplements
science.body: Peptides are short chains of amino acids that act as signals in the body. Peptide therapy is prescribed by a licensed clinician after an evaluation, which differs from over-the-counter supplements that are not individually prescribed. The peptides prescribed here are compounded and are not FDA-approved. Whether any option is right for you is a clinical decision, and results vary.

faqs.question: Do I need a doctor's prescription for peptide therapy?
faqs.answer: Yes. All clinical peptide protocols are prescription medications. You will consult with our licensed medical doctor who evaluates your health and orders bloodwork before prescribing your custom plan.

faqs.question: What does the doctor-guided peptide program include?
faqs.answer: Your program includes direct medical consultations with a board-certified doctor, baseline blood testing, custom compounded peptides prepared by a licensed pharmacy, and ongoing check-ins. Compounded peptides are not FDA-approved.

faqs.question: How are peptide treatments administered?
faqs.answer: Most peptide protocols use tiny, virtually painless subcutaneous injections using micro-needles (done at home or in clinic). Some peptides are also available as oral capsules or nasal sprays based on doctor recommendations.

faqs.question: How fast will I see results from peptide therapy?
faqs.answer: Timelines vary by person and by protocol. Your provider will monitor your progress over the first several weeks. Results vary.

faqs.question: Can I combine peptides with TRT or hormone therapy?
faqs.answer: Some patients use peptides alongside TRT or hormone therapy. Whether combining them is appropriate is a clinical decision that your provider makes after reviewing your history and labs.

faqs.question: How do I get started with peptide therapy?
faqs.answer: Getting started is simple! Call our clinic today at (727) 476-8966 or click 'Book Your Doctor Consultation' online. Our doctor will review your health, order any necessary bloodwork, and start your custom healing plan.

faqs.question: Are compounded peptides FDA-approved?
faqs.answer: No. The FDA does not review compounded medications for safety, effectiveness, or quality before they are marketed. These products are prepared by a licensed pharmacy for individual patients when a licensed clinician determines that an FDA-approved product does not meet that patient’s specific clinical needs. Your provider will explain the options available to you and the risks of each.
